cells.tense: You are finishing things at the moment they are actually finished.
cells.ask: Pick the one ending you have been circling and set a date for it this week, then tell one person the date.
cells.core:
You finish things when they are finished, and not a minute early. When something has run its course you can feel it, and you clear it without dragging it behind you or cutting it down before its time. What you build afterward holds because the old thing was allowed to end first, and that order is doing more for you than any plan you could draw up.

It gives the people around you something steady to stand on, too. They can count on you to say when a thing is over instead of letting it fade. Keep that hand — the fair read of when it is done — and let it decide one more thing than you usually hand to it. Nothing about this needs to be loud to be real.
cells.sheetLine: You end things on time, and what you build afterward holds.
cells.verb: ending what cannot continue so the next thing can start
cells.place: where you decide what holds and what gets built

cells.tense: You are bracing against a future you cannot write in advance.
cells.ask: Name one thing you were about to end this week and hold it open for seven days without touching it.
cells.core:
You are already living in a version of what comes next, and from there you keep clearing the ground ahead of you. Something gets uncomfortable and it is gone before anyone can say what it was worth. The shaking feels like freedom from where you are sitting, and what it is mostly doing is keeping you one step ahead of anyone who might reach you.

A fairer read of when a thing is done includes the other people standing in it. The ending you are about to make is not only yours to time. Let one thing stay standing long enough to find out whether it belongs to you at all. What you keep and what you release both get decided from the same steady place, and that place is still here when the bracing stops.

cells.tense: You are keeping something in place that has already stopped moving.
cells.ask: Choose one thing you have stopped using but kept in place and clear it out today — the object, the file, or the standing invitation.
cells.core:
Keeping something in place after it stops moving is what you are doing, and you are calling it loyalty. Nothing comes through it and nothing goes out, and you hold the arrangements exactly where they were. The structure you are good at making has gone tight around something that is no longer in it.

Direction comes back through your own feet, not through deciding how you feel first. Do one physical thing where the old arrangement sits: take it out, move it, give it away. Whatever you want to feel about it can arrive later — what matters now is that your hands move before your certainty does. You have organized harder problems than this one.

cells.tense: You are already ending something and have not said so out loud.
cells.ask: Write down one thing you have quietly stopped investing in and read the line to someone you trust within the next day.
cells.core:
The ending is already underway in what you have stopped putting time into, what you no longer defend, the arrangements you keep in place out of habit. You are accounting for it as things simply being busy, or the season, or other people's choices, when the pattern running underneath is yours.

The structure you are good at making is the thing to lean on. Give the ending a shape you can look at — a line, a date, a sentence with your name in it — and let that shape carry what you have not yet said. You do not have to feel finished to say a thing is finishing. You only have to name what you already stopped doing.
cells.sheetLine: You have already started ending this. Say it and let it count.
